children: Definedge raises Rs 22 crore in pre-Series A funding, taking total capital raised to Rs 30 crore as it expands trading and wealth-tech platforms
Fintech and brokerage startup Definedge has raised Rs 22 crore in a pre-Series A funding round, taking its total funding raised to Rs 30 crore, as per a media report.
The round saw participation from existing backers Nitin Agarwal and D Prasad, along with new investors Anant Jain and Sachin Kasera.

Definedge had previously raised its first institutional and angel funding round in November 2025, with participation from Hemant Luthra, Ajay Srivastava, D Prasad, Nitin Agarwal and Madhusudan N Sarda.

The fresh capital will be used to strengthen infrastructure and low-latency execution, scale its trading products Zone and Opstra, and expand Algostra into a no-code retail algorithmic trading platform.
The startup also plans to develop Momentify from a systematic investing tool into a broader wealth creation platform.

Founded in 2021 by Prashant Shah and Rajesh Badiye, Pune-based Definedge operates a wealth-tech ecosystem comprising more than 14 platforms, including Opstra, Zone, Algostra, Momentify and Gurukul. Its products cover trading, investing, research and learning for retail participants.
Definedge is targeting Rs 5,000 crore in assets under management through Momentify over the next 24 months. The platform has already crossed Rs 1,000 crore in AUM, according to the company.
The startup also plans to expand its Gurukul learning platform and increase its technology, service and operational capacity to support a larger customer base.

Definedge said its user base grew 125 per cent over the past 14 months and increased tenfold over the past 36 months. The company is also focusing on artificial intelligence-powered platforms including Momentify and Algostra.
Indian fintech startups raised about USD 2 billion across 106 funding rounds in the first half of 2026, representing a 42 per cent year-on-year increase.
In the brokerage and wealth-tech segment, platforms including Groww, Zerodha, Angel One, Upstox and Dhan operate alongside newer platforms targeting younger and first-time investors.

Sahi raised USD 33 million in 2026, while Trackk and Zomint were reported to be in funding discussions. Navi raised USD 100 million from Prosus in its first institutional funding round, while wealth-management platform Centricity raised USD 27 million during the same period.

The segment is also expanding into international equity investing. Groww, Zerodha, Angel One and Upstox have received approvals from the International Financial Services Centres Authority to facilitate international equity investments through GIFT City.
